title: CAP-MANIFEST-ID-V1 ADM-DOMAIN successor registry (current)
standing: Normative CURRENT successor of delivery.v4 capabilityManifestIdentity valueDomains. Selected by identity-and-evidence section 3 - the committed-CVE1 admission paragraph, which names this document as the effective value-domain / ADM-DOMAIN registry in place of delivery.v4 valueDomains within this declared scope - and listed by native-evidence section 11 (Identity domains authored here). The inherited delivery.v4 and fact-plane.v1 BYTES are unchanged and remain the historical record; this document does not rewrite them. Scope: it extends exactly one registry - the relation domain - with native-evidence section 4.4 unresolved-edge, and states each relation ladder so a rung from another relation cannot pass. Everything else is reproduced verbatim.

recipe.committedBytes: the exact CVE1 encoding of the CapabilityManifestV1 value
recipe.codecSeparation: CVE1 is the CAPABILITY MANIFEST encoding and has nothing to do with the relation PAYLOAD codec. Relation payloads are canonical JSON C under foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json; the superseded relation payload CBOR profile and CVE1 are three different things and none substitutes for another.

closedProperty: EVERY SCALAR IN A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS EITHER BOUND TO A NAMED REGISTRY OR DECLARED OPEN, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE. A bound scalar is admitted only if its value is a member of its registry, compared by EXACT NFC UTF-8 BYTES -- no case folding, no alias, no trimming, no prefix match, no normalisation of any kind. An OPEN position is one this schema declares open, with the declaration itself standing as the record that no registry constrains it. A position that is neither bound nor declared open is a schema defect, and it is inadmissible until it is one or the other.

RELATION-DOMAIN-V2.source: fact-plane.v1#relationRegistry.relations (12, inherited verbatim) extended with native-evidence section 4.4 unresolved-edge. A provider declaring the new relation as a capability could not previously be expressed in a capability manifest at all, which made it unrepresentable in a PlanId input.

RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.rule: The value bound to a relation KEY must be a rung of THAT relation ladder. A rung that is a member of another relation ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token.
RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.order: Weakest-first, matching the authority exactly. These arrays were previously sorted alphabetically while still declaring the inherited ladder as their source, which reversed calls, imports and references relative to the ladder they name. That was harmless only because this registry is consulted for MEMBERSHIP alone; anything reading it as an ORDER would have inverted the comparison and let a syntactic fact satisfy a demand for a resolved rung.
RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.mirrorOf: foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry/relations[].ladder, the single ladder authority. Drift-checked exactly and in order; this registry publishes no independent ladder value.

PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1.source: delivery.v2#platformMatrix.supported[].platformId (5, measured) and delivery.v2#platformMatrix.bestEffort[].platformId (2, measured), plus the aggregate token 'all-supported'.
PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1.inheritedVocabularyIsBROADERThanTheSelec: This domain is the INHERITED delivery vocabulary, reproduced verbatim, and it is deliberately not narrowed here. The selected product promises exactly FOUR machine platform ids - linux-x86_64-gnu, linux-aarch64-gnu, macos-aarch64, macos-x86_64. The OWNING authority for that selection is the security unit's S8 platform table, which is the one machine platform vocabulary, together with native-capability-matrix.v2.json platformFamilies, which carries the identical four ids. S8 is also where Windows is excluded: it names Windows among the populations outside the selected support population, for which the core refuses rather than degrades. (The blind consumer-B v5 review cited admission-and-qualification section 5 item 1 for that exclusion; that citation is not where the selection lives. The review's own bytes remain the historical record and are not edited - this entry simply cites the actual owner.) windows-x86_64-msvc, windows-aarch64-msvc and linux-x86_64-musl are therefore members of this ENCODING domain and of no product promise.
PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1.whatAMemberOfThisDOMAINDoesNOTGrant: Admitting a platformId here admits a capability manifest SCALAR under ADM-DOMAIN. It is not a platform admission, not a qualification lane, not a supported population and not a licence to run anywhere: platform admission is the security owner's (S8 platform_admit and the signed PlatformProfileSetV1) and a request naming an unselected platform is refused there, whatever a manifest declared. A provider declaring a capability for an unselected platform therefore obtains no product capability on it; nothing downstream reads this domain as a support claim.
PLATFORM-ID-DOMAIN-V1.accountedOpenItem: delivery.v4 already discloses the mismatch as DUD-V4-9. This entry repeats that accounting in the current source so a reader of the successor registry alone does not have to recover it from the historical artifact. Narrowing the inherited members is NOT done here: it would change an inherited encoding domain, and therefore the admissibility of historical committed bytes, to fix a documentation gap.

CapabilityManifestV1.source: delivery.v2#capabilityManifestSchema.CapabilityManifestV1.required, verified on the live bytes at the digest in recordedInputs

ProviderCapability.closedIsNEW: delivery.v2 declares closed only on CapabilityManifestV1.

ProviderCapability.relations.shape: a JSON object mapping relationId to resolution
ProviderCapability.relations.whyClosedIsFALSEANDNOTMISSING: because a MAP has no key set to be exact about. Writing `closed: false` here is not a permission to carry undeclared keys -- DL-DOM-1 admits its keys against a named registry, which is a STRICTER gate than a key set would be, since a key set is fixed at authoring and a registry is maintained by the surface that owns the relations. It is the field delivery.v3's catch-all had no way to read, which is why it refused everything.
ProviderCapability.relations.order: NONE -- CVE1 sorts map entries by key bytes, so there is no order to rule on, and a duplicate key cannot reach the encoder under the section 7.5 parse hook.

recordShape.everyReachableObjectTypeIsCLASSIFIED: FOUR reachable object types, THREE records and ONE map, and the census is exhaustive over the four live manifests and the three synthetic vectors. The retained checker walks each admitted manifest and fails the run if it reaches an object that is in neither list.

x-opensip-digest-law: capabilityManifestId is retention `derived`: it is recomputed from the retained committed bytes, never trusted.
traversalOrder: DECLARED, because a diagnostic that names 'the first violation' without a declared traversal is not reproducible. Within ADM-ORDER: (1) for each providers[i] in index order, platformIds; (2) for each coverageForAbsent[i] in index order, relationIds; (3) providers; (4) coverageForAbsent. Every vector in this document publishes its COMPLETE violation list in this order, so nothing depends on which violation is first.

ADM-TYPE.statement: Every scalar is admitted by EXACT JSON TYPE before its content is compared. schemaVersion is a JSON integer -- a boolean is not an integer, a float is not an integer, a numeric string is not a number -- and every other declared scalar is a JSON string. The type assertion is the gate; content comparison happens only after it passes.

ADM-CLOSED.statement: EVERY REACHABLE RECORD IS CLOSED, AND A MAP IS NOT A RECORD. Every JSON object reachable from a committed CapabilityManifestV1 -- the record itself, every element of every declared collection, every value of every declared map, and every object a later successor adds at any depth -- is either a RECORD or a MAP, and the schema says which by what it declares for it. A RECORD declares a KEY SET: it carries EXACTLY that key set, each key exactly once, with no undeclared member. A MAP declares a KEY DOMAIN: it carries no key set, closure does not apply to it, its keys are admitted by DL-DOM-1 against that domain, and its VALUES are governed by this property recursively -- so a map of records is closed at its records and A MAP WHOSE VALUES ARE SCALARS CLOSES NOTHING. A reachable object type that declares NEITHER a key set NOR a key domain is a schema defect and is inadmissible until it declares one; permissiveness is never the default.

ADM-DOMAIN.statement: EVERY SCALAR IN A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS EITHER BOUND TO A NAMED REGISTRY OR DECLARED OPEN, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE. A bound scalar is admitted only if its value is a member of its registry, compared by EXACT NFC UTF-8 BYTES -- no case folding, no alias, no trimming, no prefix match, no normalisation of any kind. An OPEN position is one this schema declares open, with the declaration itself standing as the record that no registry constrains it. A position that is neither bound nor declared open is a schema defect, and it is inadmissible until it is one or the other.

ADM-ORDER.statement: DL-ORD-1. Every ordered collection in a COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 is already in its declared canonical order -- strictly ascending by the unsigned bytewise comparison of its declared sort key's NFC UTF-8 bytes. A committed manifest that is not is REJECTED, with domainReasonCode RELEASE.CAPABILITY_MANIFEST_NOT_CANONICAL. It is never sorted into shape by a consumer.

admission.inheritedVerbatim: All four inherited gates are carried into the current entry point, not only the extended relation domain. ADM-TYPE is the exact JSON type assertion before any content comparison (a boolean is not an integer); ADM-CLOSED is the closed required key set; ADM-DOMAIN is the registry membership below; ADM-ORDER is strict ascending UNIQUE order in the declared traversal order, so a duplicate is an ordering violation and not merely an unsorted list.

declaredOPEN.CapabilityManifestV1.schemaVersion: OPEN. ADM-TYPE fixes the JSON TYPE (integer, exactly); no artifact fixes the VALUE set. The only live value is 1.
declaredOPEN.CapabilityManifestV1.profile: OPEN as a registry, and NOT free: DL-CUST-3 requires it to equal the owning ProfileEntry's profileId, so its domain is fixed by the release rather than by a registry. Recorded here so the census has no silent member.
declaredOPEN.ProviderCapability.providerId: OPEN. No provider registry exists in this corpus.
declaredOPEN.AbsentCapability.providerId: OPEN. Same position as above, on the other record.

declaredOPENRule: A declared OPEN position is bound by ADM-TYPE and by nothing else: it is still TYPED, and no registry is invented for it. CapabilityManifestV1.profile is OPEN as a registry yet not free - DL-CUST-3 binds it to the owning ProfileEntry profileId - so typed/domain admission and the release custody join are different acts and this document keeps them apart. Neither a provider registry nor a language registry is minted here.

decoderBounds.standing: CVE1 decoding is bounded and total-refusing.
decoderBounds.note: Depth and item counts are bounded before recursion, so a hostile committed artifact cannot exhaust the decoder. Trailing bytes, unknown tags, non-NFC text, duplicate keys and unsorted map keys all refuse; nothing is repaired.
